title: The Uncharted Monsoon
premise: Salvage diver Lena Zhou is hired quietly to recover a black box from a wreck the navy refuses to acknowledge. A dying prospector named Ansel trades her a hand-drawn map of the Serein River's forbidden headwaters for a promise to deliver a sealed tin to a woman named Mara — and the tin turns out to hold proof that the wreck, the mine upstream, and the navy's silence are one conspiracy. Hunted by the mining consortium's fixers and shadowed by a disgraced naval investigator who may be ally or trap, Lena and her crew fight upstream through rapids, jungle, and betrayal to reach the source. At the headwaters Lena must choose between selling the proof for the money that could buy her crew's survival or exposing it and losing everything she has measured her life in miles to protect. She chooses exposure, at a cost that redefines what she inherited and what she owes.
about_author: I. M. Nystrom is the pen name of a former maritime surveyor who spent a decade charting rivers in Southeast Asia before turning to fiction. They write from a houseboat with unreliable internet and a firm belief that maps are promises waiting to be broken.

chapters.title: The Wreck Nobody Names
chapters.summary: Lena Zhou dives a classified wreck off the coast, recovering a data core she was never meant to see, and notices her navy liaison lying about the ship's registry. Told from Lena's POV. Establishes her mile-counting philosophy and her crew's precarious finances. Emotional beat: unease — the first crack in a story she was told to stop asking about.

chapters.title: A Trade in Salt Air
chapters.summary: In a port bar, dying prospector Ansel Kade offers Lena a hand-drawn map of the Serein headwaters in exchange for a promise: deliver a sealed tin to a woman named Mara in the river town of Vessel. Lena, needing money, accepts but plans to renege. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: reluctant hope tangled with the guilt of a promise made to a dying man.

chapters.title: What the Tin Contains
chapters.summary: Curiosity wins; Lena opens the tin and finds survey records linking the wreck to an illegal mining operation at the river's source — and a navy cover-up. That night, strangers search her boat. POV: Lena, with a brief interlude from crewmate Dev. Emotional beat: dread crystallizing into purpose; the map is now a weapon she cannot put down.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: Lena's crew runs the lower Serein by night to avoid consortium patrols, and they find Mara — who reveals Ansel was her father and the records her family's stolen inheritance. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: grief becoming resolve; two inheritances, one river, and the first real alliance.

chapters.title: The Man from Naval Intelligence
chapters.summary: Disgraced investigator Elias Rook intercepts the boat, claiming he wants the truth exposed but demanding the records as collateral. Lena bargains, keeps copies, trusts no one. POV: Elias. Emotional beat: wary, charged ambiguity — is he a lifeline or the consortium's longest reach?

chapters.title: Devil's Throat
chapters.summary: The crew shoots the river's worst rapids to outrun a consortium gunboat; Dev is badly injured and the fuel cache burns. Lena must decide whether to turn back or push on with less than half her crew fit. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: the price of survival made physical; loyalty tested against arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Town That Sells Silence
chapters.summary: In a mining-town waystation, Lena discovers half the river is on the consortium's payroll — including a face she trusted. Rook's loyalties fracture publicly when he refuses an order to kill them. POV: Elias. Emotional beat: corruption revealed as a whole economy, not a villain; trust rebuilt in the smallest coin.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Lena and Mara reach the headwaters: a flooded open-pit mine poisoning the river, guarded and officially nonexistent. They photograph everything, but the alarm sounds as consortium forces converge. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: awe and horror fused — the forbidden source is a wound.

chapters.title: Miles Run Out
chapters.summary: Cornered at the pit's rim, Lena must trade the originals for her crew's lives or broadcast the proof and lose everything. She triggers a live transmission of the survey records as Rook holds off the fixers, and Dev pays a final price covering their escape. POV: alternating Lena and Elias. Emotional beat: the climax — sacrifice as the only currency left.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the scandal breaks; the navy dissembles, but the river has witnesses now. Lena buries Ansel's map at the source's edge, keeps only the promise, and measures her life in years again. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution — inheritance redefined as obligation, survival as something you owe forward.
